Non-parametric bootstrap

pk_bootstrap.Rd

Resamples subjects with replacement (optionally stratified, for example by sampling design), re-estimates the model from the final estimates of the run and stores the estimates of every replicate in models/<run>/eval/bootstrap.rds. Replicates are saved after each fit (or after each batch if parallel = TRUE), and a repeated call continues from the stored replicates (resume = TRUE).

Usage

pk_bootstrap(
  run,
  n = 200,
  strata = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  est = NULL,
  seed = 1,
  parallel = FALSE,
  resume = TRUE,
  fit_fun = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE,
  proj = NULL
)

Arguments

run

A completed run (reference or id).

n

Total number of replicates wanted.

strata

Name of a subject-level column to stratify the resampling by.

data, fit_fun, quiet, proj

See pk_run().

est

Estimation settings for the replicates. Default: SAEM with 250 burn-in and 250 EM iterations.

seed

Base seed; replicate b uses seed + b.

parallel

Use future.apply::future_lapply()?

resume

Continue from stored replicates?

Value

A tibble with one row per replicate (invisibly).

Details

By default the replicates are estimated with SAEM, which is robust to the starting values and does not need an OFV. For parallel execution install future.apply and set a plan, for example future::plan("multisession"). Only the main process writes to the project; the workers return results.
